name: Altan
notes: The two Alta languages, 'very distinct languages one from the other' (Reid 1994: 450). Under Proto-Northern Luzon (Reid 2006's Cordilleran), which Reid's tree (2006: 4) divides into Altan, Meso-Cordilleran, Arta, Ilokano and Northern Cordilleran. Reid (1994: 452-455) relates the Alta languages to Meso-Cordilleran (Central and Southern Cordilleran) by their l < *R and man- prefix, but notes that they keep forms and pronouns that all other Meso-Cordilleran languages replaced; no Meso-Cordilleran node is entered. No proto-language is reconstructed; Glottolog has no node for the pair.

name: Northern Alta
region: Baler River valley, Aurora, and Dingalan; Nueva Ecija
notes: Negrito language; most speakers are bilingual in Tagalog (Reid 1994: 450). Data from Reid's field work (1987; Reid 1988b). Coordinates from Glottolog 5.4.

name: Southern Alta
region: South-eastern Nueva Ecija to the boundary of Aurora and Nueva Vizcaya
notes: Negrito language, strongly influenced by Tagalog and in contact with Umiray Dumaget (Reid 1994: 450, 455-462). Coordinates from Glottolog 5.4.

name: Arta
region: Addalem River near Aglipay and Maddela, Quirino
notes: Fewer than fifty families of Negritos (Reid 1994: 462). About 29% of Reid's 512 items are unique to Arta, and it keeps only 26.9% of Blust's 200 PMP basic items (p. 463). Many loans from Ilokano, Gaddang and Casiguran Dumagat (Tables 19-21).
